classification.difficultyReason: Solve two different intersection problems, select the points identified by the diagram and use their coordinates as perpendicular triangle dimensions.

content.prompt: The circle $x^2+y^2=1$, the parabola $y=x^2$ and the line $y=x$ are drawn on the same axes. Let $A$ and $B$ be the points of intersection of $y=x$ with the circle and parabola, respectively. $XA$ and $YB$ are drawn perpendicular to the $x$-axis.

spec.description: Three equation-driven curves with A and B in the first quadrant, perpendicular feet X and Y and right-angle marks. O is retained because it names a vertex in the requested triangles. Source blue and red are mapped to standard palette accents.
spec.mathematics: Unit circle centred at O; parabola y=x²; line y=x; A=(1/√2,1/√2), B=(1,1), X=(1/√2,0), Y=(1,0). Coordinate values are construction data and are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied figure identifies the required intersections without displaying their coordinates or triangle areas.

answer.worked:
For $A$, substitute $y=x$ into the circle equation:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+x^2&=1\\2x^2&=1\\x^2&=\frac12\\x&=\pm\frac1{\sqrt2}.\end{align*}$$
The diagram selects the first-quadrant intersection, so $x=y=\frac1{\sqrt2}$ and $A=\left(\frac1{\sqrt2},\frac1{\sqrt2}\right)$.

For $B$, equate the expressions for $y$:
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=x\\x^2-x&=0\\x(x-1)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }x=1.\end{align*}$$
The diagram selects the non-origin intersection in the first quadrant. Thus $x=y=1$ and $B=(1,1)$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the area of triangles $OAX$ and $OBY$.

answer.short: $\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OAX)=\frac14$ square unit; $\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OBY)=\frac12$ square unit.
answer.worked:
The perpendicular segments give $OX=XA=\frac1{\sqrt2}$ and $OY=YB=1$.
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OAX)&=\frac12\times OX\times XA\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OAX)&=\frac12\times\frac1{\sqrt2}\times\frac1{\sqrt2}\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OAX)&=\frac14\text{ square unit}.\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OBY)&=\frac12\times OY\times YB\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OBY)&=\frac12\times1\times1\\\operatorname{Area}(\triangle OBY)&=\frac12\text{ square unit}.\end{align*}$$
